Processor-derived2..8 bounds registered reusable buffer slots per process. If no reusable entry remains and that count is exhausted, allocation uses alloc_no_reuse rather than rejecting. Oversized requests also allocate directly. This fallback obtains committed process virtual memory and returns no reuse cookie; its release frees that allocation. Thus the reuse count does not bound simultaneous active allocations or aggregate committed bytes.

Cached bookkeeping participates in process notifications and collection. This is a reuse/reclamation lifecycle, not a complete cross-process resource admission ledger. Its source does not establish finite completion of every active caller or cap every kernel/cached/request allocation.

Work preparation can lock user buffers and allocate request/work-item state before posting to CriticalWorkQueue. Posting marks the IRP pending. The routine may complete it, repost through ordinary/BestEffort IOQ or retain pending/ignore status. The inspected path has no local global active-work byte/count reservation or finite work-duration deadline. Dispatcher joining alone therefore does not establish this independent native asynchronous work has drained.
